subject: Order form: commitment phasing, credit flow & tax responsibility
messages:
From: James O'Neill <james.oneill@atlascloud.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Order form scheduling & tax treatment

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement wanted me to confirm a couple of items before we issue the PO:

- Atlas typically requests net-45 invoice terms for annual commitments; can Redwood accept net-45 for this order form (total committed $600k across 12 months)?
- We have an internal requirement to split the advance credit: 25% upfront, 75% invoiced monthly against usage. Does Redwood require minimum-commit invoicing up front, or can we structure it as a credit pool?
- For tax: Atlas is requesting that Redwood accept the withholding responsibility in our territory (Ireland). We can provide a tax certificate if needed. Who at Redwood handles VAT/withholding evidence?

I'll attach our standard PO template. If you need a legal contact to accelerate redlines, loop them in and we'll aim for signature this week.

Thanks,
James
James O'Neill
Senior Procurement Manager
Atlas Cloud
attachments: Atlas_PO_789.pdf

-----Original Message-----
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: James O'Neill <james.oneill@atlascloud.com>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2026 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Order form scheduling & tax treatment

James — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses below; I will loop in finance and legal for details and a redline: 

- Net terms: We typically run net-30 for hosted and dedicated deals, but net-45 isn't a dealbreaker if the customer provides a PO and we set the billing cadence appropriately. Need finance sign-off (cc'ing Ben).
- Credit structure: We can support a credit pool model; the order form needs to reflect an advance credit allocation and a mechanism to draw-down monthly. If Atlas wants 25% upfront as a nonrefundable activation portion and 75% as a refundable (or draw-down) credit, we can model that in the order form. Marketing of numbers will affect MRR recognition — I'll let Marissa and Ben flag any accounting constraints.
- Withholding/VAT: We accept tax certificates and will work with legal to add a clause assigning withholding responsibility. Kimberly — can you propose wording for tax handling and any EU/Ireland-specific evidence we should collect?

I'll prepare a mutual action plan and share a redline back to you by EOD Monday.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, James O'Neill <james.oneill@atlascloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 May 2026 12:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Order form scheduling & tax treatment

James / team — looping in Legal. A few points from our side re: draft order form and tax: 

1) Net terms: Legal is fine to accept net-45. We will add an early-payment incentive clause (1% if paid within 15 days) to protect cashflow if that helps Atlas.

2) Credit flow / minimum commit: We need explicit language that defines: (a) the upfront "activation" payment (25%) as applied to the committed annual minimum, (b) the credit pool draw-down mechanism, and (c) any refund or shortfall reconciliation at the end of the term. We will provide two sample clauses (prepay vs. credit-pool) so Atlas can pick.

3) Tax / withholding: If Atlas requests to withhold under local law, Redwood will accept provided Atlas supplies a government-issued tax residency certificate plus a signed statement accepting responsibility for withholding and remitting to the local authority. If withholding applies, we will gross-up invoices or adjust credits per the order form appendix (we will propose language).

4) Attachments: Please send the Atlas PO in native PDF and the tax cert as a high-confidence scanned doc.

We will produce a redline of the Order Form with the two commercial options by Monday COB. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, James O'Neill <james.oneill@atlascloud.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Order form scheduling & tax treatment

James — Ben on Payments/Finance. Couple operational clarifications: 

- Invoices: If Atlas prefers monthly invoices against usage (draw-down), we will issue monthly invoices net-45 and apply the draw-down credit on receipt. If the upfront 25% is nonrefundable, it will be invoiced as an advance payment upon signature.
- PO routing: Please confirm the remit-to entity on the PO. Redwood has multiple legal entities — for EU customers we sometimes route through Redwood EU Ltd; for Atlas (EIRE) we'll need to confirm whether they require Redwood EU or Redwood Inc on the invoice.
- Tax evidence: tax certificate (PDF) is sufficient; our tax team will review and confirm whether gross-up is required.

If you can confirm remit-to and attach the tax cert, I can provision the billing schedule and a sample invoice for Atlas to approve.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

If Redwood requires a nonrefundable activation, we need to see the redline.

1) Legal (Kimberly) to deliver two redline options for the Order Form by EOD Tuesday: (A) refundable credit pool approach; (B) activation + draw-down with limited refund.
2) Finance (Ben) to produce billing schedule and sample invoices showing net-45 cadence and credit draw mechanics by EOD Tuesday.
3) Commercial (Marissa) to confirm recognition and any commercial adjustments if Atlas elects refundable vs nonrefundable credit.
4) James / Atlas to confirm final remit-to legal entity (Redwood EU Ltd vs Redwood Inc) in PO header and confirm who will perform withholding.

I'll coordinate a short call Wednesday morning to finalize the redline if needed. Thanks everyone — let's aim to have an executed order form by Friday so procurement can issue the first invoice.
